objective: Equity book v1.4 candidate: does an out-of-sample ML composite of the same 22 slow theme inputs plus log size (M2 GBDT rank-mean of LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost on the 21-session book-aligned label; M3 DKKM random-Fourier-feature ridge SDF, P = 4,000, on the 5-session book-aligned return), or an equal blend of M0 with either, raise the offset-median net Sharpe of the unchanged v1.2 construction (U3000) by >= 0.10 in both the recent 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and the stress-ML 2019-01-02..2023-08-31 windows, with annual expanding refits from 2019, a 43-session embargo and the same costs, and does it survive the paired test, account layer, placebo and family-19 DSR tier?
target_regime_and_horizon: Same as v1.2 (hypotheses.md section 7 there): US equities in the research U3000, weekly 5 tranches, decision at the close of D, fill at the close of D+1, 21-session alpha horizon for M2 and 5-session holding for M3. The composite is meant to be regime-robust, so it must improve both the recent window 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and the stress-ML window 2019-01-02..2023-08-31 (the first refit needs two years of data, so 2017-10..2018-12 has no out-of-sample prediction). Validity to 2026-12-31 with the v1.2 book; annual refits continue only if the candidate is kept.
existing_solution_comparison: Published methods are reused, not invented: M2 is the T-17 GBDT ensemble (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost settings frozen 2026-09-30, rank-mean as T-17's ENS), M3 is the DKKM 2024 random-Fourier-feature ridge SDF (eq. 6 and 9, gamma grid of footnote 12), the inputs are the S1 library's 22 theme inputs (JKP-style themes). Off-the-shelf products (JKP factors, AQR funds) do not give a point-in-time stock-level score for our universe and costs, so the gap is local: whether these methods beat the equal-weight composite after our costs in 2019-2026, which no source measures. The design doc (section 5) already preregistered M2/M3 for v1; Stage 2b was cancelled only because the v1 construction failed, and the v1.2 construction now reaches tier P1.
remaining_evidence_gap: Out-of-sample (annual expanding refits) net-of-cost value of a nonlinear composite of the same slow inputs inside the v1.2 construction, in the 2024-2026 window and in 2019-2023, against the equal-weight composite that is already at tier P1; plus the turnover of nonlinear scores (M0 weekly rank autocorrelation 0.983).
negative_experiments_checked: t20261002_book_v12: learned weights lost to equal weights (M1_U3000 recent net Sharpe 1.389 vs M0 1.506), and the book's return is mostly style premium (specific -1.2% a year), so a residual-return target would discard the premium; this contract therefore uses a book-aligned (beta-hedged, industry-demeaned) label. T-20260930-17: price-volume ML stress RankIC 0.020-0.059, ensembles +0.006..+0.012 over LightGBM. T-20261002-24: ml_pv residual IC recent t 0.5-1.8, not admitted. T-19: pure price-volume long-only ML books closed. t20261004_book_v13_tc: E3 used a raw (not scale-free) paired difference; this contract uses the vol-matched form and states power before freezing. RF1 M0X (T-19 prediction as a tenth theme) was not run (data constraint), so no ML composite has been evaluated in a v1.x construction.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Identical to v1.2 / T-25 R6: make_cost_fn('close') at E = $1M (half-spread + square-root impact + 0.5 bp fees per side, ETF branch for SPY), borrow 25 bp a year on short notional, full rebalancing at each tranche refresh, D+1 close fill; 2x cost replay on the same paths reported. Account layer (selected candidate only): whole shares, $100 minimum order, Alpaca Reg T margin, delisting bound -30% long / 0 short.
stop_condition: Stage A: no candidate's simplified weekly gross Sharpe beats M0's in both windows, or the label-permutation check fails -> stop, keep M0. Stage B: no candidate meets E1 (+0.10 offset-median net Sharpe vs B0r in both windows), E2 (>= 4/5 offsets per window), E4 (|OLS| and |Dimson beta| <= 0.15) and E5 (permutation check clean) -> keep M0 and close ML composites for the v1.2 construction until new inputs exist.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Stage A of brief T-20261004-02: build the weekly training matrix and daily prediction features locally (run_capped 1.2G), train M2 (3 GBDTs) and M3 per refit year 2019..2026 on Modal (8 shards, 4 CPU, 8 GiB, 30 min each, worst case about $1), label-permutation retrain (LightGBM and M3), then the simplified weekly gross long-short test against M0 on offset-0 dates.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one candidate's simplified weekly gross Sharpe exceeds M0's in both the recent 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and the stress-ML 2019-01-02..2023-08-31 window, and both permutation-label models stay within +/- 2 standard errors of zero (|Sharpe| <= 2 / sqrt(years)) in both windows.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: No candidate beats M0's simplified gross Sharpe in both windows: the ML composites of the same slow inputs add nothing before costs, so Stage B is not run and ml_contribution_pass is recorded false.

sources.claim: Didisheim, Ke, Kelly and Malamud (NBER w33012, Sept 2024): an SDF built from P random Fourier features of rank-standardized characteristics, S = [sin(gamma Z w), cos(gamma Z w)] with w ~ N(0, I) and gamma drawn per feature from {0.5, ..., 1.0}, factors F = N^-1/2 S'R and ridge Markowitz weights lambda(z) = (zI + E[FF'])^-1 E[F], earns out-of-sample SDF Sharpe ratios near 3.7 with high complexity and light shrinkage (360-month rolling window, monthly, 1993 onward), about 2.6 times the low-complexity models; the full-sample result is heavily influenced by microcaps, but mega- and large-cap-only SDFs still reach about 1.6 and 1.8, above FF6's 0.74. All gross of trading costs.
sources.core_claim: Random-Fourier-feature ridge SDFs with P >> T earn out-of-sample SDF Sharpe near 3.7 (1993 onward, gross), about 2.6x low-complexity models; mega/large caps alone about 1.6/1.8 versus FF6 0.74.
sources.applicability: Exact form of M3 (eq. 6 and 9, gamma grid footnote 12, N^-1/2 scaling footnote 10), applied to our 23 slow inputs weekly.
sources.limitations: 130 JKP characteristics, monthly data and 30-year windows versus our 23 inputs, weekly data and 1-8 years of training; gross of costs; no industry neutralization; microcap-driven headline numbers.
sources.independent_replication: AQR Alternative Thinking 2024 Q4 reports the same 'virtue of complexity' pattern on value/momentum, FF5+momentum and defensive signal sets (50-100% gross Sharpe improvement, 65% in liquid large caps); same research group, so not independent.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks (JKP), monthly, OOS 1993 onward, 360-month rolling windows; all size groups

sources.claim: AQR Alternative Thinking 2024 Q4 'Can Machines Build Better Stock Portfolios?': complex random-feature models built on economically motivated signals improve out-of-sample gross Sharpe by 50-100% over the simple linear model in three applications (value and momentum; FF5 plus momentum; defensive signals), 65% when restricted to liquid large caps (footnote 17); the complex model's return stream is 'highly additive' to the simple model; adding just two noisy predictors to the value-momentum model cuts performance by about half (Exhibit 7, 1963-2019). Results are gross of transaction costs.
sources.core_claim: Complex models on economically motivated signals improve out-of-sample gross Sharpe 50-100% (65% in liquid large caps) and are highly additive to the simple model; two noisy predictors halve performance.
sources.applicability: Fixes the input set to economically motivated themes and motivates the M0+ML blends.
sources.limitations: Practitioner note, hypothetical gross results, long samples since 1963; the cost question is explicitly left open (footnote 11).
sources.independent_replication: None independent; DKKM 2024 is the same group. BSW 2022 is contrary evidence after costs in large caps.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks, 1963-2019, monthly; also liquid large caps

sources.claim: Barroso, Saxena and Wang (Oct 2022, EFMA 2024) 'Calm Your Portfolio': in the 500 largest US stocks, mean-variance portfolios built from improved return forecasts (Fama-MacBeth, feed-forward neural network, conditional autoencoder, IPCA, nonparametric additive models) and improved covariance estimators do not beat the passive value-weighted portfolio after costs; with risk targeting plus turnover penalties all 32 transaction-cost-managed portfolios beat it, and the best net Sharpe ratios (1.10-1.20) come from the linear Fama-MacBeth forecasts with the daily sample covariance, not from the ML forecasts; without short sales none significantly beats the passive strategy.
sources.core_claim: In the 500 largest stocks, ML forecasts do not beat linear Fama-MacBeth forecasts after costs; turnover-penalised risk-targeted portfolios reach net Sharpe 1.10-1.20 with the linear forecasts.
sources.applicability: Contrary prior: lowers the chance that M2/M3 replace M0; supports keeping M0 in the blends and the paired-test requirement for replacement.
sources.limitations: Preliminary working paper; 500 largest stocks, monthly mean-variance optimization rather than a rank-weighted beta-hedged book; ML models trained by the authors, not production-grade.
sources.independent_replication: Consistent with Avramov, Cheng and Metzker (2023): ML profits concentrate in microcaps and distressed firms and shrink under economic restrictions.
sources.market_and_period: 500 largest US stocks, monthly, characteristics from 1964, OOS decades to about 2020
